full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 262

A Technology Co., Ltd. v. A Culture Media Co., Ltd. — dispute over unfair competition

(Discussed and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court; released on August 28, 2025)

Keywords: Civil; unfair competition; data set; data transfer; operational interests

Ruling Gist

When the operational interests formed by a network platform operator in a data set are infringed, it may request the people's court to provide protection in accordance with law. For conduct that, without authorization, obtains and provides relevant data to the public, substantially substitutes for the network platform operator's products or services, disrupts the market competition order, and damages the lawful rights and interests of the network platform operator or other right holders, the people's court may apply the relevant provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC and find that it constitutes an act of unfair competition.

Basic Facts

A Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "A Technology") is the operator of APP A. A Culture Media Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "A Culture") is the operator of APP B. Between November 2018 and May 2019, 50,392 short videos on APP B were identical to short videos on APP A, and the short videos contained codes proprietary to APP A. Among the short videos involved in the case, there were 19,079 registered user nicknames and user avatars. Of these, 15,924 were identical to those on APP A; 127 instances of comments had the same content, order, and punctuation as those on APP A. Upon investigation, about 40% of the short videos were original and constituted works; the remaining short videos had certain value but were not original and constituted video recordings.

A Technology filed a lawsuit on the ground of unfair competition dispute, alleging that A Culture, without authorization, directly captured and transferred the data involved in the case from APP A and displayed and disseminated them on APP B, constituting an act of unfair competition. Therefore, A Technology requested the court to order A Culture to eliminate the adverse effects and compensate for economic losses of RMB 40 million.

A Culture argued that the short videos involved in the case fall within the scope of protection under the Copyright Law of the PRC, and that A Technology has no rights or interests in the short videos uploaded by users on APP A. APP B developed by A Culture is a platform for users to upload short videos, and its business model is legitimate.

Judgment

The Beijing Haidian District People's Court rendered a civil judgment ((2019) Jing 0108 Min Chu No. 35902) on December 31, 2020, ordering A Culture to publish a statement in a non-center position of the *China Intellectual Property News* to eliminate the adverse effects for A Technology in respect of the unfair competition acts involved in the case; and ordering A Culture to compensate A Technology for economic losses of RMB 5 million. After the judgment was pronounced, A Culture appealed. The Beijing Intellectual Property Court rendered a civil judgment ((2021) Jing 73 Min Zhong No. 1011) on March 16, 2023: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

There are two main issues in dispute in this case: First, what rights and interests does A Technology have in the data set formed by aggregating short videos, user comments, and user information? Second, whether A Culture's conduct of obtaining and using the data involved in the case constitutes an act of unfair competition.

1. A Technology has operational interests in the data set involved in the case. The Copyright Law protects original intellectual achievements, as well as audio and video recordings that have certain value but are not original. In this case, the original short videos involved constitute works, and the remaining short videos constitute video recordings; both are protected by the Copyright Law. However, A Technology, as the data aggregator, is not the producer of the short videos involved. Moreover, its aggregation of the short videos involved was only classified according to common categories on network platforms such as "videos, live streaming, music," and the selection and arrangement did not reflect originality, nor did it constitute a compilation work. Therefore, when others massively transfer the short videos aggregated on its platform, A Technology cannot claim rights or seek legal remedies under the Copyright Law.

Nevertheless, the data set involved in the case was collected and aggregated by A Technology. Apart from short videos, it also includes registration information (nicknames and avatars) published by users in accordance with the user agreement when uploading and using short videos, user comments, etc. In summary, the data set involved was formed through the interaction between users and the platform, where users followed platform rules and utilized the technical support provided by the platform. The data set is large in scale and has high commercial value. A Technology has made substantial investments of human, material, and financial resources in the formation and accumulation of the data set, attracting a large volume of user traffic through its operations, thereby generating additional economic value from the data set independent of individual short videos. Consequently, the operational interests arising from A Technology's holding, use, and operation of the short video data set shall be protected by law. Of course, this does not affect the rights of the short video producers under the Copyright Law.

2. A Culture, without authorization, obtained and provided the relevant data to the public, which was sufficient to substantially substitute for the products and services provided by A Technology, and thus constitutes an act of unfair competition under law. In their production and business activities, business operators shall follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, and comply with laws and commercial ethics. Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "For the purposes of this Law, 'acts of unfair competition' refer to acts committed by business operators in their production and business activities that, in violation of the provisions of this Law, disrupt the order of market competition and damage the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers." Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC (Fa Shi [2022] No. 9) provides: "Where a business operator disrupts the order of market competition, damages the lawful rights and interests of other business operators or consumers, and the circumstances are not covered by the provisions of Chapter II of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the Patent Law, the Trademark Law, the Copyright Law, or other laws, the people's court may apply Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to make a determination."

In this case, A Culture, without authorization, captured and transferred a large amount of user information, short videos, and user comments from the data set involved and used them on APP B, resulting in a high degree of homogenization of content between APP B and APP A. Network users could view the same content through APP B without using APP A, substantially substituting for the products and services of APP A operated by A Technology. Consequently, A Culture's conduct of capturing and transferring the data involved and using it on APP B damaged A Technology's operational interests.

In summary, A Culture's conduct involved in the case disrupted the order of market competition and damaged the lawful rights and interests of other business operators and consumers. However, this conduct does not fall within the acts of unfair competition specified in Chapter II of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and A Technology's operational interests in the data set involved could not be protected under the Copyright Law or other laws. Therefore, the people's court, applying Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law in accordance with law, found that A Culture's conduct involved in the case constituted an act of unfair competition.

It should be noted that on June 27, 2025, the 16th Session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress made the second revision of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, adding a special provision in Article 13, paragraph 3 on acts of unfair competition infringing data rights. Accordingly, after the revised Anti-Unfair Competition Law takes effect on October 15, 2025, the people's court shall apply Article 13, paragraph 3 and relevant provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law to accurately determine whether the relevant conduct constitutes an act of unfair competition.

Related Laws

Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC

Articles 3, 15, and 44 of the Copyright Law of the PRC (in this case, Articles 3, 14, and 42 of the Copyright Law of the PRC as amended in 2010 apply)

Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC (Fa Shi [2022] No. 9)
